subject: Winter et al. (1997)
object: In affected members of a family with monilethrix, Winter et al. (1997) identified a mutation in the type II hair keratin hHb1 that changes glutamic acid-403 to lysine (Glu403Lys). This residue sits in the helix termination motif and corresponds to Glu410 of hHb6. The authors suggested that this site is a mutational hotspot in these closely related type II hair keratins.

subject: Winter et al. (1997)
object: Winter et al. (1997) found the common hHb6 Glu410Lys mutation in affected members of a second, unrelated monilethrix family and in one isolated patient.

subject: Winter et al. (1997)
object: Winter et al. (1997) described monilethrix as a rare dominant hair disorder. The hair is beaded (moniliform) because the hair shaft thins at regular intervals, and it is highly prone to excess weathering and breakage.

subject: Winter et al. (1997)
object: Winter et al. (1997) noted that hHb1 and hHb6 are largely expressed together in the cortical trichocytes of the hair shaft. They concluded that monilethrix is a disease of the hair cortex.

subject: Winter et al. (1998)
object: Winter et al. (1998) described a French family with monilethrix that showed a particularly variable phenotype. One infant had pronounced dystrophic alopecia, follicular keratosis, and clear-cut moniliform hair. A second infant had no hair loss, and the moniliform hair was detectable only by electron microscopy. An adult family member had no symptoms detectable clinically or by electron microscopy but had clear historical proof of the disease.

subject: Winter et al. (1998)
object: In a French family with monilethrix, Winter et al. (1998) identified a glu402-to-lys (E402K) mutation in the type II hair keratin hHb1 (KRT81). The mutation affects another highly conserved glutamic acid residue (Glu106 of the 2B subdomain) in the EIATYRRLLEGEE helix termination motif. Before this report, pathogenic mutations in hHb6 and hHb1 had been limited to Glu413.
